_about: Probe bank: short, general statements about products and pitches. The Brain Library asks a brain's trainer to agree/disagree with these (and with claims extracted from ideas). Written for BrainPrint; not from any dataset.

claims.text: I would happily pay a monthly subscription for a tool that saves me time.
If it is not free to start, I will not try it.
A product that takes a percentage of each sale is fair because I only pay when I earn.
I trust AI to handle my money-related paperwork.
When a pitch says 'AI-powered', I get more interested.
Most 'AI' startups are just hype wrapped around a simple feature.
I would connect my bank account to a new app if it saves me hours.
Data privacy matters more to me than convenience.
A pitch that starts with a real customer story is more convincing than one that starts with features.
Technical buzzwords in a pitch make the company sound more credible.
Concrete numbers, like 'saves 5 hours a month', convince me more than adjectives.
Early traction with real users matters more than the size of the market.
I only care about ideas that could become very large markets.
Products that help local small businesses deserve support.
Reducing food waste is a problem worth paying to solve.
I would pay a bit more for a product that is better for the environment.
Half-price deals on leftover goods are attractive to me.
I do not mind picking something up in person if it is close by.
I am happy to get push notifications for nearby offers.
Admin work like receipts and taxes is the worst part of freelancing.
I prefer to do my own taxes rather than let software decide categories.
If something can be automated, I want it automated.
I abandon apps that need more than a few minutes to set up.
Security certifications like SOC 2 make me trust a product.
A tool must integrate with what I already use, or I will not switch.
I am wary of buying from a brand I have never heard of.
Seeing that others like me use a product makes me want to try it.
A clear mission matters more to me than a long feature list.
The more features a product has, the better.
A startup asking for a lot of money sounds more ambitious and serious.
I want to know how a startup makes money on each customer.
Who the founders are matters more than the idea itself.
A short pitch is better than a long detailed one.
A bit of humor in a pitch makes me remember it.
Two-sided marketplaces are hard businesses to build.
I would rather use a mobile app than a website for everyday tools.
